question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,[\operatorname{sin}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-0)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\sqrt{2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]_{\pi /4}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}(0-(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})) \\  & =\frac{{\sqrt{2}}^{2}}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
